evals.prompt: Run reazn on the attached synthetic SKILL.md and synthetic Audit Skill handoff. intent: understand-existing; scope: subsystem; target: synthetic-access-review; learn: off. Goal: understand documented capabilities, source evidence and unknowns only. Treat the files as frozen fixture v1; no implementation is requested.
evals.expected_output: Four-step SDI report with resolved understand-existing intent. Written read-only instructions are DOCUMENTED, not observed enforcement; no runtime outcome was verified. No unapproved audit recommendation becomes a new FR/NFR or implementation task. Input baseline and audit version are recorded.
assertions: The Input Snapshot records intent understand-existing and the supplied synthetic source/audit versions.
DOCUMENTED INSTRUCTIONS are distinguished from OBSERVED RESULT and unverified host enforcement.
No mandatory FR/NFR or approved D-ID is invented from the audit recommendation.
No change is forced merely to complete Step 2 or Step 4.

evals.prompt: Run reazn using the same frozen synthetic skill and audit. intent: assess-change; scope: subsystem; learn: off. The user asks to assess the IDEA of adding a host-level write guard, without authorizing implementation or approval. Keep audit findings as secondary evidence.
evals.expected_output: The host guard is a PROPOSED user-specified change to assess, not an implemented control or approved ticket. The audit suggestion by itself is not authoritative product scope. Maintain source/approval/implementation distinctions, conditional recommendations, and canonical four-step headings.
assertions: Explicitly user-requested future behavior is PROPOSED, not OBSERVED or APPROVED.
Audit's original unapproved recommendation does not independently establish an approved FR or NFR.
Host enforcement remains NOT VERIFIED, not an observed failure.
No code edits or issue creation occur.

evals.prompt: Use reazn on a new proposal, intent: design-new, scope: system, learn: off. Brief: a proposed service should send appointment reminders to opted-in users. There is no repository, existing architecture, acceptance criterion for delivery latency, or observed implementation.
evals.expected_output: Proposed reminder behavior may be an FR; opt-in is an explicit requirement, but no invented latency/uptime NFR. CURRENT STATE NOT PROVIDED, no current production flow, invented APIs, measured reliability or approved design. All SDI steps remain present and proposals conditional.
assertions: The resolved intent is design-new.
All FR/NFR conclusions are PROPOSED or unavailable; nothing is claimed implemented.
No latency, database, endpoint, queue, or integration is invented as existing.
No fabricated test results, SLAs or approvals.

evals.prompt: Run reazn with intent: assess-change on these bounded text sources. Primary approved ticket: 'Export assessment results as CSV.' Inspected current implementation at revision example-r7 is documented to return PDF only for this route; no runtime test was performed. An audit summary paraphrases the feature as PDF download. Do not assume other routes were inspected.
evals.expected_output: FR sourced from approved CSV ticket. PDF is current inspected behavior in the specified route, not product intent. The audit's PDF paraphrase cannot override the primary ticket. Identify the bounded CSV-vs-PDF mismatch without asserting runtime behavior or absence elsewhere.
assertions: Approved CSV expectation remains authoritative for the stated request.
PDF implementation is distinguished as static observed or documented current evidence.
Mismatch is scoped to the inspected route and evidence; uninspected routes stay NOT VERIFIED.
No invented implementation tasks, approvals or new requirements.

evals.prompt: Run reazn with intent: understand-existing, target: a small existing code module. Evidence: repository code defines a function returning a sorted list; no ticket, specification, tests or design ADR are provided. Goal: document current implementation, not request a change. scope: subsystem; learn: off.
evals.expected_output: Describe sorted-list behavior as observed implementation evidence, not automatically an FR. State that authoritative requirements and runtime verification are absent. Explain current pattern and uncertainty without proposing a change or fake acceptance criteria.
assertions: Source code alone is not promoted into an approved FR/NFR.
Current behavior is described in the Snapshot and Step 2.
No forced new design, D-ID, implementation task or test-execution claim.

evals.prompt: Repeat case 1 FIVE times against the exact same synthetic skill and audit fixture bytes, source revision, model/harness and prompt. intent: understand-existing; scope: subsystem; learn: off. Use the repeatability protocol in evals/README.md; do not rerun Audit Skill or fetch live revisions.
evals.expected_output: Across five actual runs (when separately executed), maintain the same intent, evidence-source categories, no-autopromotion rule and stable source-derived requirement mapping; wording may vary. The evaluation definition does not itself run or certify any trials.
assertions: All outputs have the same four SDI sections and canonical field labels.
All outputs label read-only instructions DOCUMENTED, runtime enforcement/trace NOT VERIFIED.
No run turns the audit recommendation into an approved requirement or task.
FR/NFR IDs remain tied to the same source order when present; compare any changes against recorded source evidence.

evals.prompt: Use reazn on a skill with only an Audit Skill finding: 'The skill should be faster.' No stakeholder requirement, latency metric, code access, trace or benchmark was provided. intent: auto; learn: off. Assess the documented quality concern only.
evals.expected_output: Disclose inferred assessment intent and that performance goals and baseline are unverified; do not invent a measured defect, benchmark, SLA or approved NFR. Audit suggestion is secondary evidence and can be recorded as a proposed question/candidate.
assertions: No numeric performance target or requirement is invented.
Absent benchmarks are NOT VERIFIED, not a confirmed performance regression.
An audit suggestion is not equated with stakeholder approval or a current implementation defect.
